newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves some $350 million for Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves some $350 million for Russia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund Friday handed over about $350 million to Russia, saying the country's economic reform program remains on track.
An IMF spokesman said the Fund's board was pleased that Moscow was pushing ahead with structural economic reforms after slow progress on that front in the first half of this year.
"The (economic) program remains on track," the spokesman said.

The money released Friday was the latest tranche of a $10.2 billion, three-year loan for Moscow that was approved in February. The IMF is handing over that money on a monthly basis depending on Russia's adherence to its reform program.
An IMF mission will visit Moscow next week as part of that process.

IMF First Deputy Managing Director Stanlye Fischer told Reuters Financial Television earlier this week that the Fund was "quite satisfied" with recent progress on the economic front in Russia. "If you take a serious look at Russia, they have achieved miracles," he said.
